description: Lives in the corner of my porch

The organism appears to be a typically shaped arachnid having 8 long legs and an elongated body with a pointed abdomen. Most of its body is a deep brown shade with sections of light brown on its legs. With its legs, the organism is ~3 centimeters by ~3 centimeters. Its abdomen is ~4 millimeters long and ~2.5 millimeters wide. It has a glossy surface with no distinguishable patterns visible. The organism was found crawling on an exterior wall of my father's tire shop in Florida. The organism's features and its location indicate that it is Crossopriza lyoni, otherwise known as the Tailed Cellar Spider. According to the Iowa State University Department of Entomology, "The only cellar spider in North America that has the pointed abdomen... is Crossopriza lyoni" (Iowa State University Department of Entomology, n.d.). Cellar spiders, particularly the Tailed Cellar Spider, are commonly found in, "temperate or subtropical areas" (Iowa State University Department of Entomology, n.d.).

References
Iowa State University Department of Entomology. (n.d.). Family Pholcidae - Cellar Spiders. https://bugguide.net/node/view/9608
